name: Detective's Clue Board
mechanic: A row of animal characters each want one item; the child reads/hears 2-4 picture clues ('The cat does NOT want the ball', 'The dog wants something round') and taps which item belongs to which character, eliminating possibilities until each is uniquely assigned. A clue 'lights up' green as the placement satisfies it.
why_distinct: This is a true logic-grid / constraint-satisfaction-by-elimination engine — the answer is forced by AND-ing negative and positive clues, not by matching a picture to its pair. Closest neighbor is match-pairs (template) and sort-home: separation is that NO single clue gives the answer; the child must cross-reference clues and use process-of-elimination. Distinct from logic-deduction-08 (analogy) which is one-step pattern transfer, not multi-clue cross-referencing.
fun_no_competition: The 'aha!' when the last clue snaps everything into place and all the characters cheer with their item; clue cards literally glow as you satisfy them so progress feels like real detective work.
interaction: tap-then-tap (select item, tap character slot) or drag item to character
character_world: A friendly detective owl with a magnifying glass helps a group of woodland friends figure out whose lost item is whose.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — clue evaluation is simple boolean logic over a small attribute table; DOM tiles + CSS glow states; TTS for clue read-aloud.
asset_idea: stub: colored boxes for characters + item icons. CA5: owl detective with magnifying glass, 4-5 woodland-friend characters with distinct silhouettes, item set (ball/bone/hat/cup), green glowing clue-card frame.

name: No Two The Same (Constraint Garden)
mechanic: A small grid (3x3 or 4x4 latin-square) of garden plots; the child plants flowers so that no row and no column repeats the same flower. Tapping an empty plot cycles/places a flower; an illegal placement makes that flower wilt and shake (rule violated), a legal one blooms. The child reasons forward from given starter flowers.
why_distinct: Constraint-propagation (mini-Sudoku/Latin-square) — the skill is deducing the only legal flower for a cell from row+column constraints. Different from sort-home (one correct bin per item) because legality depends on the WHOLE row/column, not the item itself. No template covers grid-wide mutual constraints. Separation from logic-deduction-01: there the constraints are external clues; here they are emergent from placement (uniqueness rule).
fun_no_competition: Flowers bloom with a little sparkle when the whole garden is legal; wilting-then-perking-back-up on a mistake is gentle and funny, never punishing — pure trial-and-reason satisfaction.
interaction: tap to cycle/place; drag from a small flower palette
character_world: A garden-gnome gardener who 'loves variety' and gets delighted when every row and column is all-different.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — Latin-square legality check is trivial; CSS bloom/wilt animations; small fixed grids keep it K-3 sized.
asset_idea: stub: colored circles in a grid. CA5: gnome gardener, 3-4 distinct flower sprites (each with bloom + wilt frame), soil-plot grid backdrop, sparkle burst for a solved garden.

name: Guess My Rule (Sorting Machine)
mechanic: A two-bin sorting machine has already sorted several example items (e.g. apple→left, truck→right, banana→left, bus→right). The child must INFER the hidden rule, then sort 3-4 NEW items correctly. Getting them right reveals the rule label ('Things you can eat!'). The child can ask for one more example before committing.
why_distinct: The skill is rule-INDUCTION from examples, the inverse of sort-home. In sort-home the category is stated; here it is HIDDEN and must be deduced from worked examples. No template has the child infer the classifier. Distinct from logic-deduction-01 (given clues) — here the child generates the hypothesis themselves.
fun_no_competition: The detective thrill of cracking the secret rule; the machine 'whirs' and the rule label flips up with a fanfare when the child proves they figured it out — the reward is being RIGHT about the hidden logic.
interaction: drag new items to a bin; tap 'show me one more example'
character_world: A quirky robot sorting-machine with googly eyes that 'has a secret rule' and is tickled when you guess it.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — rule is a stored attribute predicate; examples and test items pulled from vocab attribute tags; DOM bins.
asset_idea: stub: gray machine box, two bins. CA5: googly-eyed robot machine with two chutes, conveyor of mixed item icons (food/vehicles/animals), flip-up rule-label sign.

name: True, False, or Why (Math Statement Court)
mechanic: A character states a math claim shown with pictures ('3 + 2 = 4' with three apples plus two apples; or '5 is greater than 8'). The child judges TRUE or FALSE — and on FALSE, taps the picture/numeral that PROVES it (e.g. taps the extra apple, or taps which number is actually bigger). The proof-tap is required, so the child must reason about WHY, not just guess.
why_distinct: Two-stage truth-evaluation + justification — distinct from any choice-tap template because a binary guess isn't accepted; the child must locate the evidence. The 'why' tap instantiates reasoning about equality/comparison rather than computing an answer. No template does claim-falsification.
fun_no_competition: Playing 'judge' is empowering for a 6-year-old; a wrong claim gets a silly buzzer and the proof spotlight, a true claim gets a gavel-bang of approval — the delight is catching the character's mistake.
interaction: tap True/False, then tap the proving evidence
character_world: A wise tortoise judge in a tiny wig presides over a 'math court' where playful characters make claims that may be true or sneaky-false.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — statements are data {expr, truthValue, evidenceTarget}; equality/comparison check is arithmetic; tap targets are DOM elements.
asset_idea: stub: text statement + counter dots, two buttons. CA5: tortoise judge with gavel, witness-stand characters, picture-equation props (apple groups, big/small numerals), spotlight + buzzer/gavel effects.

name: Which One Breaks the Rule (Odd-One-Out With a Reason)
mechanic: Four items share a property except one. The child taps the odd one — THEN must tap WHICH attribute makes it odd from 2-3 reason-cards ('because it has no corners', 'because it is not red'). Both the odd item AND the correct reason must be selected; a wrong reason for the right item is gently corrected.
why_distinct: Standard odd-one-out only asks WHICH; this requires articulating WHY via an explicit attribute, making the reasoning explicit and instantiating attribute-classification. Different from logic-deduction-04 (judging a claim's truth) and from sort-home (binning). The reason-card layer is the key separation from a plain choice-tap.
fun_no_competition: The satisfying click of 'I found it AND I know why'; the odd item does a sheepish wiggle and the matching reason-card stamps with a checkmark — naming the reason out loud (TTS echoes it) feels like being clever.
interaction: tap odd item, then tap the reason-card
character_world: A puzzled penguin professor who points at the group and asks 'one of these is different... but can you tell me WHY?'
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — items carry attribute tags; odd-item and reason are precomputed data; two-step tap gating in plain JS.
asset_idea: stub: four shape/item tiles + reason text buttons. CA5: penguin professor with pointer, attribute-rich shape/object set (some with/without corners, varied colors), reason-cards with little icons (corner/color/size).

name: Balance Scale Detective
mechanic: A two-pan balance shows blocks; one pan tips. The child must deduce a relationship — e.g. 'the box is heavier than the ball' — and answer a question ('put the heaviest thing on the bottom shelf' or 'which is lightest?') or make the scale balance by adding the deduced number of unit-blocks. Transitive reasoning across two weighings ('A>B and B>C, so...').
why_distinct: Transitive/comparative deduction from observed states — the child infers an ordering they were never directly told, then acts on it. No template uses a physics-state (tilt) as the clue source. Distinct from logic-deduction-04 (symbolic claims) because the evidence is the visual balance, and from comparison apps because two weighings must be CHAINED.
fun_no_competition: Watching the scale tip and settle is inherently delightful; the 'aha' of chaining two weighings to know the order without ever weighing A against C directly; a balanced scale gives a satisfying gentle chime and level wobble.
interaction: drag objects/unit-blocks onto pans; tap to answer the ordering question
character_world: A friendly mouse shopkeeper weighing mystery parcels who needs help figuring out which is heaviest.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — weights are data, tilt is CSS rotate driven by sum comparison; transitivity is precomputed for the question.
asset_idea: stub: simple beam + two pans + numbered blocks. CA5: mouse shopkeeper, ornate balance scale with springy beam, parcel/object weights, unit cube blocks, chime + level-glow on balance.

name: If-This-Then-That (Rule Robot)
mechanic: A robot follows a single visible if-then rule ('IF the shape is red, THEN it goes in the box'). A conveyor brings items one at a time; the child decides for each whether the rule fires (tap KEEP or PASS). Across a level the rule may compound ('IF red AND round'). The child applies conditional logic, not categorization.
why_distinct: Conditional rule-APPLICATION (boolean if/then, including AND) — distinct from guess-my-rule (logic-03) where the rule is hidden; here the rule is stated and the child must correctly EVALUATE it per item, including compound conditions. No template does explicit conditional evaluation. The AND-condition pushes it past simple sorting.
fun_no_competition: The robot beeps happily and stamps each item with the right decision; getting a tricky AND-rule right (an item that is red but NOT round → PASS) is a genuine logic win celebrated with confetti, no clock.
interaction: tap KEEP / PASS for each conveyor item
character_world: A cheerful factory robot that 'only follows its rule' and high-fives you when you reason like a robot too.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — rule is a predicate (single or AND of attributes); per-item evaluation is trivial; conveyor is CSS transition.
asset_idea: stub: rule banner + item on belt + two buttons. CA5: boxy factory robot with stamp arm, conveyor belt, attribute-tagged items (shapes by color/roundness), KEEP-box + PASS-chute, confetti burst.

name: Finish the Analogy (Pair Logic)
mechanic: An analogy is shown as two picture-pairs with the last slot empty: cat→kitten, dog→? . The child taps the item that completes the SAME relationship from 3-4 choices (puppy, not bone or cat). The relationship type varies (parent→baby, object→use, animal→home, big→small).
why_distinct: Relational mapping / analogical reasoning — the child must extract the RELATION from the first pair and transfer it, not match a feature. Distinct from match-pairs (template) which pairs identical/associated items with no second-order relation transfer. Closest neighbor is logic-deduction-09 (sequence rule), separated by: analogy is a 1:1 relation across two pairs, sequence is iterating a transformation.
fun_no_competition: The clean 'click' of seeing the hidden relationship — the completed analogy animates the pair connecting with a little zap, and a wise character nods 'you saw the connection!'
interaction: tap the choice that completes the analogy
character_world: A connect-the-dots fox who loves spotting how things 'go together the same way'.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — analogies are data {A,B,C, answer, distractors, relationType}; pure tap; images from vocab.
asset_idea: stub: 2x2 grid of picture slots, one empty, choice row. CA5: fox character, paired-item art sets (animal/baby, tool/use, animal/home), glowing relation-link line, zap effect on correct.

name: Crack the Pattern Code
mechanic: A short sequence follows a hidden transformation rule (shapes growing by one side, numbers +2, colors rotating, rotation by 90°). The child must INFER the rule and tap which item comes NEXT from choices — and for older grades, also tap a 'missing middle' term. The rule is never stated.
why_distinct: Sequence rule-induction with a TRANSFORMATION (not just AB-AB repeat). Distinct from existing pattern-train apps (those mostly repeat a fixed unit) because the rule is a growing/changing transformation the child must deduce. Separated from analogy (logic-08): analogy maps one relation across a pair; this iterates a rule along a sequence and may probe an interior term.
fun_no_competition: The detective satisfaction of cracking a growing pattern; the sequence 'completes itself' with a marching animation when right, and the secret rule reveals as a little tag ('+2 each time!').
character_world: A code-breaking raccoon spy decoding 'secret pattern messages'.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — sequences generated from a parameterized rule; choices include near-miss distractors; tap-only.
asset_idea: stub: row of shape/number tiles + '?' + choices. CA5: raccoon spy with decoder goggles, growing-shape and numeral tile sets, secret-message scroll backdrop, rule-reveal tag.

name: Spot the Impossible
mechanic: A scene or statement contains something that CANNOT be true (a fish riding a bicycle; '2 + 2 = 5' on a chalkboard in a real scene; a snowman at the beach in summer). The child taps the impossible/nonsense element and the game asks them to confirm with a quick reason-tap ('fish can't ride bikes' / 'that math is wrong'). Distinguishes possible-but-silly from truly impossible.
why_distinct: Anomaly detection / reasoning about real-world and logical possibility — instantiates both math-correctness checking and informational-text/world-knowledge inference. Distinct from i-spy-scene (template) which is find-a-named-target; here the target is UNNAMED and must be reasoned to be 'the thing that doesn't make sense'. Distinct from logic-04 (judge a single stated claim) — here it's a scene-embedded reasoning hunt.
fun_no_competition: Giggle-worthy 'that's silly!' moments; tapping the impossible thing makes it pop/fix itself with a giggle sound — the delight is being the one who notices what's wrong.
interaction: tap the impossible element, then tap/confirm the reason
character_world: A 'Reality Inspector' chameleon with a clipboard who 'keeps the world making sense'.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — scenes are composed layers with one tagged anomaly; reason-cards are data. Needs curated scene art but logic is trivial.
asset_idea: stub: scene with a flagged odd element + choices. CA5: chameleon inspector, several silly-anomaly scenes (fish-on-bike, beach-snowman, wrong-equation chalkboard), pop/fix animation, reason-card icons.

name: Sudoku Picture Path (Mini Constraint Grid)
mechanic: A 4x4 picture-Sudoku where each row, column, and 2x2 box must contain one of each of four pictures. Pre-filled cells constrain the rest; tapping an empty cell shows only the four pictures and the child reasons which is forced. A cell that violates a constraint shows a soft red outline; a fully legal grid blooms.
why_distinct: Classic deductive constraint-satisfaction with the box constraint adding genuine cross-region deduction. Distinct from logic-deduction-02 (Latin square, rows+cols only) by the added 2x2-box constraint, which forces multi-constraint intersection reasoning — a meaningfully harder deduction shape for grade 2. Not in any template; the existing sudoku app is operator-tooling, not a premium reasoning game with this scaffolded reveal.
fun_no_competition: The pure logic-puzzle 'click' of deducing a forced cell; soft non-punitive constraint feedback keeps it calm; the finished grid lights up region by region in a satisfying cascade.
interaction: tap empty cell → tap chosen picture
character_world: An owl puzzle-keeper who tends a 'thinking garden' grid and is delighted by a perfectly-filled board.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — 4x4 Sudoku legality (row/col/box) is simple; pre-generated solvable boards as data; DOM grid.
asset_idea: stub: 4x4 grid + four picture tokens. CA5: owl puzzle-keeper, four themed picture tokens (fruits or animals), region-divider grid styling, cascade bloom for a solved board.

name: Whodunit Story Clues
mechanic: A short illustrated mini-mystery ('Who ate the cookies?') gives 2-3 picture/text clues drawn from the story ('the thief left muddy paw prints', 'it was tall enough to reach the shelf'). The child cross-references clues against 3-4 suspect characters and taps the only one who fits ALL clues. Tapping a suspect highlights which clue rules them out.
why_distinct: Narrative inference + elimination drawn from text/illustration evidence — instantiates RL inference (using key details to answer who/what/why). Distinct from logic-deduction-01 (abstract item-assignment grid) because clues come from a STORY and require reading-comprehension inference, not just attribute matching. Distinct from spot-the-impossible (10) which is anomaly, not multi-clue elimination.
fun_no_competition: Solving the gentle mystery and watching the culprit sheepishly confess ('it was me!'); each clue you use to rule out a suspect crosses them off with a fun stamp — true detective delight, no timer.
interaction: tap a suspect; clues highlight; tap to accuse the one fitting all clues
character_world: A kid-detective duo (a curious cat and a magnifying-glass mouse) solving cozy neighborhood mysteries.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — suspects carry attribute tags, clues are predicates; elimination logic + TTS for clue read-aloud; needs illustrated suspects/scenes.
asset_idea: stub: clue list + suspect row + accuse buttons. CA5: cat+mouse detectives, 4 suspect characters with distinguishing traits (tall/short, muddy paws, etc.), cookie-jar scene, cross-off stamp + confession animation.

name: Make the Statement True (Fix the Equation)
mechanic: A math equation is shown FALSE on purpose ('4 + 3 = 6') with one element draggable/swappable — the child reasons what to change to make it true (swap the 6 for a 7, or add/remove a counter from a group). The equation only 'locks' (glows green, characters cheer) when the relationship is genuinely true. Includes choosing the right comparison symbol (<, =, >) to make a statement true.
why_distinct: Repair-to-truth — the child must reason backward from a desired truth-state to the needed change, the inverse of computing a sum. Distinct from logic-deduction-04 (judge true/false) because here the child must ACT to FIX it. No template does equation/relation repair. Instantiates the meaning of the equal sign and comparison reasoning.
fun_no_competition: The deeply satisfying moment the wobbling 'wrong' equation snaps level and glows true; the equal sign does a little balancing animation — fixing it yourself feels like solving a riddle.
interaction: drag to swap a numeral/counter, or tap to choose <, =, >
character_world: A wobbly tightrope-walking sign character who 'can't balance until the math is true'.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — truth check is arithmetic; draggable numerals/symbols are DOM; instant re-evaluation on change.
asset_idea: stub: equation with one swappable slot + numeral/symbol palette. CA5: tightrope equal-sign character, counter groups, swappable numeral tiles, <,=,> symbol tokens, balance-snap + cheer animation.

name: Even/Odd Pair-Up Reasoning
mechanic: A pile of objects is shown; the child must decide if the amount is EVEN or ODD — by pairing them up (tap to draw a 'buddy line' between two) and reasoning whether anyone is left alone. If one is left without a partner it's odd; all paired means even. Then they tap EVEN or ODD and the leftover (or lack of) is the proof.
why_distinct: Deductive even/odd via the pairing argument — instantiates 2.OA.C.3 specifically through the 'is anyone left over?' reasoning, not memorized rules. Distinct from any counting template because the child constructs the PROOF (the pairing) and reasons from a leftover. No template pairs-to-deduce a parity property.
fun_no_competition: The little objects buddy-up with happy faces; the lonely leftover one looks sad-but-cute until the child correctly calls 'ODD!' and it gets a high-five — the proof is visible and adorable.
interaction: tap two objects to pair them (draws a buddy line), then tap EVEN / ODD
character_world: A friendship-themed world where objects 'just want a buddy' and the child helps figure out if everyone has one.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — pairing tracked client-side; parity computed from count; SVG buddy-lines; simple state.
asset_idea: stub: scattered dots + EVEN/ODD buttons. CA5: cute object characters (socks/mittens that naturally pair), buddy-line connector with little heart, lonely-leftover sad-then-happy face, high-five effect.

name: Riddle Reveal (Deduce the Mystery Word)
mechanic: Three or four spoken/written riddle clues describe a hidden picture-word ('I have four legs. I say woof. I am a pet. What am I?'). Clues appear one at a time; after each, the child may guess by tapping one of 4-6 picture choices — narrowing as clues add. Wrong early guesses just dim that choice; the right answer celebrates and re-reads the clues that pointed to it.
why_distinct: Progressive clue-narrowing word deduction — instantiates vocabulary/category reasoning (using describing attributes to identify a word). Distinct from logic-deduction-12 (suspect among story characters) because here it's identifying a vocabulary concept from descriptive attributes, and distinct from i-spy (find a NAMED target) because the target is described by properties, never named.
fun_no_competition: The building suspense of each new clue narrowing it down; the 'I know it!' moment of an early correct deduction; the answer character pops out happily and the clue-trail lights up showing the reasoning.
interaction: tap a picture choice after any clue (more clues available on demand)
character_world: A riddle-loving genie/sphinx who poses gentle picture-riddles and is delighted when you reason it out.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — riddles are data {clues[], answer, distractors}; TTS for clues; tap choices; dimming logic trivial.
asset_idea: stub: clue text lines + picture choice grid. CA5: friendly genie/sphinx character, themed picture-word sets (animals/foods/objects) with attribute-rich art, clue-scroll, glowing clue-trail reveal.

name: Logic Lockbox (Multi-Clue Combination)
mechanic: A treasure box has a 3-symbol code lock. Picture-logic clues constrain each slot ('the first symbol is NOT a star', 'the second symbol is round', 'there is exactly one moon'). The child deduces the only valid combination and sets each dial, the box opening only when all clues are satisfied. Tapping a clue highlights which dial it constrains.
why_distinct: Combination deduction under multiple simultaneous constraints (a code-cracking constraint puzzle) — close to logic-deduction-01 but the answer is an ORDERED sequence with positional + global constraints (exactly-one, not-this, must-be-round), a richer constraint vocabulary. Separation from 01: 01 assigns items to characters (a matching), this fixes an ordered code from positional+counting constraints.
fun_no_competition: The treasure-hunt thrill of cracking a secret code; each dial click feels consequential, and the box bursts open with sparkles + a reward animation when the deduced combination is right — no timer, just careful reasoning.
interaction: tap each dial to cycle symbols; tap clues to see which dial they constrain
character_world: A pirate parrot guarding a treasure chest who 'only opens for clever code-crackers'.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — clues are positional/global predicates over a 3-slot code; legality check on each dial change; DOM dials.
asset_idea: stub: 3 symbol dials + clue list + box. CA5: pirate parrot, ornate treasure chest with 3 dials, symbol set (star/moon/round-gem), clue scrolls, sparkle burst + reward (gold coins) on open.
